comparator.name: Japanese Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The current Leiden catalogue confirms an ordinary 180 EC degree with disciplinary seminar choices. This example uses the Leiden-based second-year option and the thesis pathway. In year two there are 20 EC of required study and 40 EC of restricted choices: 10 EC semester-one seminar, 5 EC semester-two seminar, 5 EC restricted option, 5 EC shared Asian studies, and a 15 EC Leiden or study-abroad option. The Leiden option combines Modern Japanese 2c and a distinct shared Asian studies course. Year three contains 15 EC of specialist choices, a 5 EC Graduation Seminar and 10 EC thesis, and 30 EC open study. The alternative external research project is 30 EC and changes the open allocation; it is not included. Year-one mentorship carries zero credit. Non-curricular proficiency preparation is excluded. Current annual module descriptions establish the language and research gates; the archive is corroborating context. The current programme-specific regulation URL returned an access page.

exception.reason: UCR offers related study in comparative history, politics, sociology, literature, film and material culture. Its courses include some relevant cases, such as Chinese empires and Japanese-American incarceration. Across a full UCR programme, the advanced work would focus mainly on other regions or on general methods, with limited sustained study of Japan and East Asia. Leiden brings Japanese language, regional study and research with Japanese sources together throughout the degree. The related UCR courses offer useful starting points, but they do not form a sufficiently close alternative for this Japan-centred programme.

exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed the current 151-course reference. Actual relevant history, comparative politics, international relations and qualitative methods were credited alongside material-media, museum, comparative literary and film methods. History of Empires includes China and Media & Race includes Japanese-American incarceration within US cultural history. Psycholinguistics supplies experimental language and bilingualism methods. The history description for Researching the American Century supports substantial historical inquiry, with the current named American subject. The combined challenge reaches broad methods, some Asian cases and comparative approaches, with most advanced sustained investigations centred elsewhere. Related courses are not rejected for lack of title or qualification equivalence. See the detailed candidate assessment.

candidateAssessment.label: Japanese history, society and international relations through comparative inquiry
candidateAssessment.reason: Comparative empire, global modernity, geopolitics, international law, research methods and Asian-American history provide genuine points of contact. The available sustained investigations focus on other regions or general institutions, leaving Japan and East Asia largely a context students would have to supply independently.

candidateAssessment.label: Japanese arts, material culture and media through comparative interpretation
candidateAssessment.reason: Archaeological artifact analysis, museum interpretation, media archaeology, film adaptation and literary analysis offer substantive comparative tools. The case coverage and advanced curriculum do not sustain Japanese arts, literature and media as a degree focus.

candidateAssessment.label: Language and culture through linguistics and cultural studies
candidateAssessment.reason: Psycholinguistics provides language acquisition, bilingualism and experimental methods, and stylistics supports textual analysis. Neither offers Japanese language development, Japanese linguistic inquiry or training to interpret Japanese research sources. A wider language-and-culture proposal would combine general methods without a sustained Japan-centred core.

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden’s Japanese Studies bachelor combines Japanese language with the study of Japan’s history, society, politics, arts and media. The degree places Japan in its East Asian and global context and culminates in a research project using Japanese-language material.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers related study in comparative history, politics, sociology, literature, film and material culture. Its courses include some relevant cases, such as Chinese empires and Japanese-American incarceration. Across a full UCR programme, the advanced work would focus mainly on other regions or on general methods, with limited sustained study of Japan and East Asia. Leiden brings Japanese language, regional study and research with Japanese sources together throughout the degree. The related UCR courses offer useful starting points, but they do not form a sufficiently close alternative for this Japan-centred programme.

curriculum.routeLabel: Leiden-based second-year option and thesis pathway
curriculum.limitation: The example totals 180 EC. Year two includes four restricted choices and a 15 EC Leiden-based option. In year three, students take 15 EC of specialist choices, a 15 EC thesis pathway and 30 EC of open electives. Entry to the final seminar and thesis requires first-year completion, at least 10 EC of second-year seminars, the relevant Japanese-language components and participation in a third-year seminar. The thesis uses Japanese-language sources.

componentNotes.j1-language-a: Entry requires reading and writing hiragana and katakana.
componentNotes.j2-language-b: The block 3 course combines language production and text study. Both Modern Japanese 2a components must be passed first.
componentNotes.j2-language-c: The block 4 continuation combines language production and text study. It is taken on the Leiden-based option in place of study abroad.
componentNotes.j3-graduation: The 5 EC seminar supports the thesis and develops academic Japanese through reading, writing and discussion.
componentNotes.j3-thesis: A 10 EC supervised research thesis using Japanese-language sources. It is normally written in Dutch or English.
